forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: North Kesteven projects £533k general fund surplus as borrowing costs fall
news_drafts.lead: North Kesteven Council is projecting a General Fund surplus of £533,300 for 2026-27, driven mainly by lower-than-expected borrowing costs. The council budgeted for £2.54m in interest payments but now expects to spend only £1.92m, a saving of £617,600 built on timing of planned loan drawdowns for Lafford Homes development that concentrate borrowing into the second half of the year. Pay awards 0.3 percentage points higher than budgeted cost £51,400, and additional fuel costs add £22,800 of pressure. The surplus is being added to reserves: £233,300 to the Our Council Reserve and £300,000 to the Financial Resilience Reserve. The Housing Revenue Account, by contrast, projects a deficit of £160,700. The council is also managing capital scheme underspending of £1.8m against a budget of £10.1m, suggesting capital projects are not progressing at the pace anticipated in February.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1: DRAFT Complaints Performance and Service Report
findings.headline: Damp and mould complaints (21 cases, 76.2% upheld) triggered Ombudsman-ordered capital remedial works (HHSRS inspection and repairs), creating committed expenditure obligation.
findings.detail: Damp and mould complaints totalled 21 cases (9% of 217 complaints), with 76.2% upheld (16 of 21). One Ombudsman determination (May 2025) specifically concerned damp, mould and complaint handling. The Ombudsman 'ordered the Council to undertake a full HHSRS inspection, complete any identified works' alongside £950 compensation. The high uphold rate combined with regulatory (HHSRS) remedial requirements creates non-discretionary capital expenditure.
findings.matters: Upheld housing health & safety complaints generate committed capital remedial works; Ombudsman-ordered works are mandatory expenditure obligations.
findings.figures: 21 damp and mould complaints (9% of 217); 76.2% upheld (16 of 21)
findings.quote: The Ombudsman ordered the Council to undertake a full HHSRS inspection, complete any identified works and make a compensation payment of £950, all of which were completed within the required timescales.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1: DRAFT Complaints Performance and Service Report
findings.headline: Stage 1 investigation quality shows material weakness: 68.4% of complaints initially not upheld were subsequently upheld at Stage 2 review (13 of 19 cases).
findings.detail: The paper reports that 13 of 19 complaints not upheld at Stage 1 were overturned to upheld at Stage 2 review. This is presented as evidence of weakness: 'it also highlights the importance of continuing to strengthen Stage 1 investigations to ensure all relevant issues, evidence and customer impacts are fully explored at the earliest opportunity.' The high reversal rate indicates systemic issues in initial investigation quality or completeness.
findings.matters: High Stage 2 reversal rates drive escalation costs and create material risk of further Ombudsman referrals and compensation liability.
findings.figures: 13 of 19 initially not-upheld complaints reversed to upheld at Stage 2 (68.4%)
findings.quote: Importantly, 13 of the 19 complaints that were not upheld at Stage 1 were subsequently upheld at Stage 2 (68.4%). This demonstrates the value of the Stage 2 review process as an effective safeguard within complaint handling arrangements.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1: DRAFT Complaints Performance and Service Report
findings.headline: 14.3% of Stage 1 complaints (31 cases) breached permitted response timescales, with 60.4% reliance on extension periods indicating resource or process constraints.
findings.detail: Of 217 Stage 1 complaints, only 25.3% were resolved within the 10-working-day standard; 60.4% required extensions to 20 days; 14.3% fell outside permitted timescales entirely. The paper acknowledges 'reliance on extensions remains significant and continues to be an area for improvement during 2026/27.' Ombudsman determinations identified timescale breaches as maladministration, citing 'delays in responding to service requests' and 'insufficient communication regarding those delays'.
findings.matters: Timescale breaches create Ombudsman escalation risk and indicate potential resource constraints or process inefficiency, with precedent from two 2025/26 upheld determinations.
findings.figures: 14.3% outside permitted timescales (31 complaints); 25.3% within 10-day standard
findings.quote: Overall, 25.3% of landlord complaints were resolved within the standard 10 working day timescale, with a further 60.4% responded to within an agreed extension period, resulting in 85.7% of complaints being responded to within permitted Complaint Handling Code timescales. The remaining 14.3% were responded to outside permitted timescales.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1: DRAFT Complaints Performance and Service Report
findings.headline: Two of three Housing Ombudsman determinations upheld in 2025/26 finding maladministration, ordering £1,300 compensation and remedial works
findings.detail: Of three Ombudsman investigations completed in 2025/26, two were upheld. The first (May 2025) found 'maladministration in the Council's handling of concerns relating to windows and doors, damp and mould, and complaint handling' and ordered 'a full HHSRS inspection, complete any identified works' alongside £950 compensation. The second upheld determination (July 2025) on anti-social behaviour management found 'maladministration in both the handling of ASB reports and complaint handling' and ordered £350 compensation.
findings.matters: Upheld determinations create compensation liability precedent and reveal systemic process failures (delays, record-keeping, communication) indicating governance weaknesses beyond individual complaints.
findings.figures: 2 upheld determinations of 3 investigated; £1,300 total compensation (£950 + £350); Ombudsman-ordered HHSRS inspection and remedial works completion
findings.quote: The Ombudsman found maladministration in the Council's handling of concerns relating to windows and doors, damp and mould, and complaint handling, together with service failure relating to management of concerns about the heating system.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1: DRAFT Complaints Performance and Service Report
findings.headline: Ian Williams Ltd contractor accounted for 87 complaints (40% of all landlord complaints) in 2025/26, a notable increase from prior year, with Q4 volume indicating ongoing service delivery risk.
findings.detail: The paper reports that 87 complaints cited Ian Williams Ltd, representing 60% of all repairs complaints and 40% of all landlord complaints, described as 'a notable increase from 2024/25'. While the uphold rate has declined from 92% in Q1, volume remained elevated in Q4. The council notes: 'the volume of complaints received during Quarter 4 demonstrates that repairs service delivery and customer experience remain an area of risk and will continue to be subject to close oversight.'
findings.matters: Concentration of 40% of complaints with a single contractor represents material contract performance risk with implications for service continuity, tenant satisfaction, and contract management.
findings.figures: 87 complaints (60% of repairs complaints, 40% of all landlord complaints); Q1 uphold rate 92%
findings.quote: Of these repairs complaints, 87 specifically cited Ian Williams Ltd, representing 60% of all repairs complaints and 40% of all landlord complaints received during the year. This is a notable increase from 2024/25.
